cells.tense: You are in the clearing now, feeling your way forward with your eyes open.
cells.ask: Before the day fills up, name one thing that is over. Say it to yourself, then turn toward whatever is already stirring and take one small step with it.
cells.core:
You can feel what's coming before you can put words to it. That is what carries you into the gap left by what ended, and you go in with curiosity rather than dread. You don't rush to fill the gap, and you don't pretend it isn't there. Most people skip straight past this part.

The thing to watch is tidying the ground too fast. A new plan laid on top of something only half finished gets a false start, and it inherits the unfinished thing underneath it. So keep the ground steady until the ending has actually ended. What you're feeding right now is the slow kind of growth, the kind that holds.
cells.sheetLine: You can feel what's coming before you can name it. Let the ending finish first.

cells.tense: You will have the whole next chapter built in your head before this one has finished ending.
cells.ask: Pick one thing that is over and leave it alone for a week. When you notice yourself reaching to fill it, write down what was pulling you there, and do not act on it.
cells.core:
You are running the next chapter at full speed while the last one is still closing. It feels like vision — the picture is that vivid — but you are sketching onto a surface that hasn't settled yet. The pushing is spending the energy the ending was meant to give back.

Your body tells you when it's happening. You tighten when reality doesn't match the picture you built. That tightness is the future crowding out what's actually in front of you. Care that holds space doesn't clutch. Let the clearing stay unfinished a while longer and tend only what has already taken hold. What grows without forcing holds better than anything you build ahead of time.

cells.tense: You were standing at a door long after it had already closed behind you.
cells.ask: Ask one person a real question about what they see. Listen without sorting it, and let what lands simply land before you decide anything about it.
cells.core:
The ending happened. That much is settled. What hasn't happened is any feeling about the space it left, so instead of feeling it you went quiet inside it. The wait has no date attached, and it has stopped being about the door.

More feeling won't help here — pushing emotion into a place that is already bare just wears you out. What helps is something small and specific and real. One honest conversation. One long look at something that is actually there. When one thing becomes plain to you, the next gets easier to see, and the waiting loosens its grip. What was a sentence handed down becomes a room you happen to be in.

cells.tense: You are already clearing the ground for what comes next while calling it simply what needed doing.
cells.ask: Name one thing you have already let go of, out loud, and say what you are making room for. Then do the next small thing as if that were true.
cells.core:
The clearing is already underway. Things have ended, things have been let go, room has been made, and you file all of it under practical housekeeping. None of it feels like vision to you. It just seemed like the thing to do. But it wasn't automatic, and it wasn't inevitable. You made the call.

What calling it practical costs you is the claim. None of it registers as yours. So when you do the next useful thing, let the fact that you are making room be part of what you know about it. Quiet can connect you when it has a direction, and it isolates you when it is just a habit of not saying what's true. You are already standing in the clearing.
